description.narrative:
South Africa, Zambia. The two grassroot civil society organizations CDP and ZNWL seeks to learn from each other’s knowledge and use creative arts as a tool to strengthen their advocacy strategies to improve gender equality and to address and counteract gender -based violence (GBV). They wish to include men as part of the solution in the fight against GBV as well as incorporating the creative arts in organisational advocacy work. ZNWL has an established programme for men and boys to strengthening their capacity and competence on addressing GBV in their local community. They seek to improve this programme by learning from CDP Trust’s ArtasAdvocacy to provide more interactive and expressive art skills. CDP seek to expand men’s involvement in their advocacy programmes regarding gender equality. ZNWL will share their competence on enabling young men to raise awareness among their peers and community about the negative effects of GBV.
The 2022 project aims to continue with activities from the 2021 project, but also to carry out new results. The new components of the 2022 project are that CDP will work with three community high-schools identified in 2021 where they aim to identify boys to be trained as Agents of Change in the fight against GBV. The 6 peer educators that participated in the Men in action against Gender Based Violence –Train the trainer programme with ZNWL in 2021, will facilitate a series of classroom workshops for the identified boys. ZNWL, will focus on working with the 12 boys that were trained as change agents by CDP through the Men in Action against GBV – Art as Advocacy programme in 2021. These boys will volunteer to test the advocacy techniques by conducting community outreach/awareness activities at schools in three communities in the 2022 project. Additionally, both organizations will carry on with the work they have started in the 2021 project with moving their traditional methods of training into a digital e-learning platform.
